styles.name: Colour
styles.summary: Use GOV.UK functional colours and the refreshed palette to keep meaning, interaction states and contrast consistent across services.

styles.name: Font override classes
styles.summary: Use GOV.UK font override classes sparingly when content needs an explicit alignment, size, weight, number style or overflow treatment.

styles.name: Headings
styles.summary: Use semantic heading elements and GOV.UK heading classes to create a consistent, navigable content hierarchy.

styles.name: Images
styles.summary: Use images only for a demonstrated user need and ensure their information remains available to people who cannot see them.

styles.name: Layout
styles.summary: Use GOV.UK wrappers and grid classes to create mobile-first pages with readable line lengths and predictable responsive behaviour.

styles.name: Links
styles.summary: Use descriptive, underlined GOV.UK links for navigation and preserve their visited, hover, active and focus states.

styles.name: Lists
styles.summary: Use semantic GOV.UK lists to break information into manageable chunks and communicate whether order matters.

styles.name: Page template
styles.summary: Use the GOV.UK page template to supply the document structure, assets and shared components required for a consistent GOV.UK page.

styles.name: Paragraphs
styles.summary: Use GOV.UK body classes for readable text, with lead and small variants only when their hierarchy has a clear purpose.

styles.name: Section break
styles.summary: Use a GOV.UK section break on an hr element to create a thematic break with standard spacing and an optional visible rule.

styles.name: Spacing
styles.summary: Use the GOV.UK static and responsive spacing scales to maintain a consistent vertical rhythm and predictable component separation.

styles.name: Type scale
styles.summary: Use the responsive GOV.UK type scale so text sizes and line heights retain the tested rhythm introduced in GOV.UK Frontend 6.

styles.name: Typeface
styles.summary: Use the approved GOV.UK typeface only for eligible services and configure an appropriate alternative for services outside the GOV.UK proposition.

components.name: Accordion
components.summary: Use an accordion to let users reveal and hide related sections when showing all of the content at once would make a page difficult to scan.

components.name: Back link
components.summary: Use a back link to return users to the previous page, in its previous state, within a multi-page transaction.

components.name: Breadcrumbs
components.summary: Use breadcrumbs to help users understand and move between levels in a website with a deep hierarchy.

components.name: Button
components.summary: Use a button to let a user perform a clear action, such as saving information or continuing to the next step.

components.name: Character count
components.summary: Use Character count when a textarea has a genuine maximum number of characters or words that users need help meeting.

components.name: Checkboxes
components.summary: Use checkboxes when users can select any number of options from a visible set, including none when allowed.

components.name: Cookie banner
components.summary: Use the Cookie banner to ask for consent to non-essential cookies and confirm the choice without blocking access to the service.

components.name: Date input
components.summary: Use Date input to collect a memorable or document-based date as separate day, month and year fields.

components.name: Details
components.summary: Use details to let users reveal optional supporting information without distracting from the main task.

components.name: Error message
components.summary: Use an error message next to an invalid field to explain what went wrong and how the user can correct it.

components.name: Error summary
components.summary: Use the Error summary at the top of a page to list validation errors and link each message to the field that needs attention.

components.name: Exit this page
components.summary: Use Exit this page in sensitive services when viewing the page could put someone at risk and they may need to leave immediately.

components.name: Feedback
components.summary: Use the Feedback component to give users a consistent, low-distraction route for sharing their experience of a service.

components.name: Fieldset
components.summary: Use a fieldset and legend to group related form controls under one question or shared label.

components.name: File upload
components.summary: Use file upload when users must select and submit one or more files from their device.

components.name: Generic header
components.summary: Use the Generic header to give a public-sector service a clear branded header when it is not entitled to use the GOV.UK crown and logotype.

components.name: GOV.UK footer
components.summary: Use the official GOV.UK footer on authorised GOV.UK services for service links, licensing and Crown copyright information.

components.name: GOV.UK header
components.summary: Use the official GOV.UK header on authorised GOV.UK services to identify the site and link consistently to the GOV.UK homepage.

components.name: Inset text
components.summary: Use inset text to distinguish a short block of supporting information from the content around it.

components.name: Language navigation
components.summary: Use Language navigation to let users identify the current language and switch to equivalent versions offered by the service.

components.name: Notification banner
components.summary: Use the Notification banner to tell users about an important change or the successful result of an action.

components.name: Pagination
components.summary: Use pagination to help users move through a collection split across several pages.

components.name: Panel
components.summary: Use a panel to highlight the outcome of an important action, especially successful completion of a transaction.

components.name: Password input
components.summary: Use the Password input when users need to enter a password, with an optional progressively enhanced control to show or hide it.

components.name: Phase banner
components.summary: Use a phase banner to show that a service is in alpha or beta and give users a way to provide feedback.

components.name: Radios
components.summary: Use radios when users must choose exactly one option from a small, visible set.

components.name: Select
components.summary: Use a select when users must choose one option from a familiar list that is too long for radios.

components.name: Service navigation
components.summary: Use Service navigation beneath the GOV.UK header to show a service name and a small set of service-level navigation links.

components.name: Skip link
components.summary: Use a skip link as the first focusable control so keyboard users can bypass repeated navigation and move to main content.

components.name: Summary list
components.summary: Use a summary list to present related key-and-value facts, optionally with contextual actions or a summary-card heading.

components.name: Table
components.summary: Use a table to let users compare structured data across rows and columns.

components.name: Tabs
components.summary: Use Tabs to let experienced users switch between closely related sections of content without leaving the page.

components.name: Tag
components.summary: Use a tag to show a concise status or category that helps users scan related information.

components.name: Task list
components.summary: Use a task list to show the tasks in a multi-part service and help users understand which are complete or still need attention.

components.name: Text input
components.summary: Use a text input when a user needs to enter a short amount of text that cannot be selected from predetermined options.

components.name: Textarea
components.summary: Use a textarea when users need to enter more than one line of free text.

components.name: Warning text
components.summary: Use warning text to alert users to an important consequence of an action or inaction.

patterns.name: Addresses
patterns.summary: Help users provide an address using separate fields, an address lookup with a manual fallback, or a textarea chosen for the service’s data needs.

patterns.name: Bank details
patterns.summary: Ask for bank or building-society account details in familiar separate fields, accepting the formats people normally use.

patterns.name: Check a service is suitable
patterns.summary: Ask a short sequence of simple questions so users can learn early whether a service is suitable, what it costs or what outcome they may receive.

patterns.name: Check answers
patterns.summary: Let users review and change the information they provided before they submit a transaction.

patterns.name: Complete multiple tasks
patterns.summary: Use a task-list journey to show which tasks are required, their helpful order and each task’s current status.

patterns.name: Confirm a phone number
patterns.summary: Check that a user currently has access to a mobile number by sending a time-limited security code in a text message.

patterns.name: Confirm an email address
patterns.summary: Check that a user currently has access to an email account using a carefully designed confirmation link or code loop.

patterns.name: Confirmation pages
patterns.summary: Tell users that they have completed a transaction, give them any reference and explain what will happen next.

patterns.name: Contact a department or service team
patterns.summary: Give users complete, contextual contact information at the point they are likely to need help.

patterns.name: Cookies page
patterns.summary: Explain every cookie the service sets and let users review and change consent for categories of non-essential cookies.

patterns.name: Create a username
patterns.summary: Help users create or use a memorable unique username only after establishing that the service needs accounts.

patterns.name: Create accounts
patterns.summary: Create an account only when users need recurring access to their service data, and defer account creation until it becomes necessary.

patterns.name: Dates
patterns.summary: Help users provide or select a date using an interaction suited to whether the date is memorable, copied from a document, approximate or selected from known options.

patterns.name: Email addresses
patterns.summary: Ask for an email address in one field, explain why it is needed and accept the broad range of valid addresses users may have.

patterns.name: Equality information
patterns.summary: Collect optional equality information consistently for monitoring and public-sector equality work, separately from operational questions.

patterns.name: Exit a page quickly
patterns.summary: Provide a rapid exit action, an accessible secondary route and supporting safety content for sensitive services where discovery could put a user at risk.

patterns.name: Interruption pages
patterns.summary: Pause a journey only when users must understand unusually important information or confirm a significant consequence before continuing.

patterns.name: Names
patterns.summary: Ask for a person’s name only when needed, using the fewest fields and accepting the characters and structures real names require.

patterns.name: National Insurance numbers
patterns.summary: Ask for a National Insurance number in one short text field, helping users find it and accepting common spacing and letter case.

patterns.name: Navigate a service
patterns.summary: Use the GOV.UK header and Service navigation together when repeat users need to move among persistent areas of a non-linear service.

patterns.name: Page not found pages
patterns.summary: Return a clear page when a requested URL does not exist and help users recover without blaming them or exposing technical jargon.

patterns.name: Passwords
patterns.summary: Help users create, enter and reset secure, memorable passwords without obstructive restrictions or unsafe recovery journeys.

patterns.name: Payment card details
patterns.summary: Collect card details in a familiar order only when an approved payment platform cannot meet the service need.

patterns.name: Phone numbers
patterns.summary: Ask for a phone number only when needed, accepting the formats, prefixes and separators people normally use.

patterns.name: Question pages
patterns.summary: Ask one thing per page using the page heading as the form label or legend and a simple continue action.

patterns.name: Recover from validation errors
patterns.summary: Validate only information the service cannot use, then explain what is wrong and how the user can fix it without losing their work.

patterns.name: Service unavailable pages
patterns.summary: Tell users when a service has been deliberately closed temporarily or permanently and explain when it returns or what they can do instead.

patterns.name: Start using a service
patterns.summary: Start a public-facing UK government service from an agreed GOV.UK content page that explains the service and links into it.

patterns.name: Step by step navigation
patterns.summary: Prototype an end-to-end GOV.UK content journey as ordered expandable steps linking to the guidance and transactions needed to complete it.

patterns.name: There is a problem with the service pages
patterns.summary: Tell users about an unexpected service failure, preserve their work where possible and give a useful recovery or contact route.
